headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 13 of the 31 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Western Maine. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Some lingering showers and cooler weather is expected across the region today following a cold front. Mostly dry and seasonable conditions are expected through the weekend into the start of next week.
Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend.
Two fronts with little moisture or forcing will offer low end chances for rain early next week, before becoming dry and warm.

ALY.excerpt:
) There is an elevated risk for fire spread today for areas within and immediately adjacent to the Hudson River Valley, western MA and northwest CT due to dry fuels combined with gusty winds and lowering relative humidity.
) Dry weather is expected this weekend through the middle of next week with increasing chances for rain later in the week.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure continues to dominate the weather into next week. Expect mainly dry conditions and no significant weather impacts. Chances for rainfall may increase toward the end of next week.

BUF.excerpt:
) Cooler and dry today behind the front.
) Another extended period of dry weather and above average temperatures this weekend into early next week.

PHI.excerpt: Generally tranquil weather is expected to prevail through at least the beginning of next week.

CTP.excerpt:
) Fire weather concerns today
) Dry and mild conditions to start November

RLX.excerpt: ) Mostly dry through the weekend, then precipitation chances return to the area during the new work week.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:22}} to {{t:51}}, with up to {{s:0.5}} of snow and gusts near {{w:41}} up top.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 23).

NWS Burlington forecasters, Friday 7:26 AM: "Some lingering showers and cooler weather is expected across the region today following a cold front. Mostly dry and seasonable conditions are expected through the weekend into the start of next week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly wetter than normal. Wet and mild often means rain below the summits.
